The cork was sealed with dark wax, the paper inside brittle as dried sea grass. He carried it back to the warm glow of the lighthouse kitchen, set it on the scarred wooden table next to his half-empty mug of chamomile tea, and carefully unrolled the page. The wobbly handwriting was dated 1952, from a 10-year-old girl who’d tossed the bottle from a cross-bay ferry, writing she hoped the finder would send a letter back to her small coastal town. Elias smiled, pulled out his fountain pen, and sat down to write his reply.", "w02": "凌晨四点的城市尚未完全苏醒，街灯晕着暖黄的光，斜斜落在空无一人的柏油路面上。远处高架上偶尔驶过夜班的货运卡车，轰隆的声响很快消散在穿巷的风里。沿街的早餐铺刚拉开卷闸门，蒸笼的白汽漫出来，裹着发面的温香。路边的梧桐叶沾着夜露，被风卷着轻轻滚过人行道，整座城市在薄凉的夜色里缓慢呼吸，静候第一缕朝阳爬过天际线。", "w03": "- Recursion is when you solve a big problem by breaking it into tiny, identical copies of the same problem, just smaller each time.\n- For example, if you want to count all the books on a tall shelf, you count the first book you reach, then use the same trick to count every book left on the shelf.\n- You always stop when you hit the tiniest, simplest version of the problem that doesn’t need any more breaking, so you never loop endlessly in circles."}
